name: Explorex
long_description:
Explorex — The Memory Layer for Physical Commerce

~90% of Indian retail happens in person, yet offline venues have no memory of their customers. Restaurants run on disconnected tools, and every visit ends with zero data captured. Explorex fixes this by owning both sides of the dining transaction.

At the center is Elite, our consumer app that is redefining how people dine out. Diners see live table availability, browse dynamic menus, order, and self-checkout instantly — no waiting, no interruptions. Behind it sits our infrastructure stack: Bridge OS (the full-stack restaurant operating system), Clyro (WhatsApp-native CRM), and ReserveX — all feeding a single behavioral data layer.

That data layer is what makes Explorex fundamentally different. Delivery platforms only see orders. We capture real-world, in-venue behavior — what people order, how long they stay, how groups behave, how menus perform, how experiences shape spending. Because we operate the restaurant OS and the consumer touchpoint, this data is irreplicable.

We're now building Elara, an AI dining concierge that turns this data into real-time decision-making — factoring intent, context, availability, and historical behavior. This moves us beyond discovery into becoming the intelligence layer for offline commerce.

Today, Explorex powers 250+ partner restaurants and 3M+ diners across Bangalore and Hyderabad, processing 8M+ transactions annually (18M+ lifetime), and operates at breakeven.

Explorex is not a SaaS tool — it is the infrastructure layer for offline dining, with AI and consumer experience at its core. Think Shopify for restaurants, on its way to becoming the UPI of restaurant operations.

question_answers.question: How did your company get started? (i.e., How did the founders meet? How did you come up with the idea? How did you decide to be a founder?)
question_answers.answer:
Pritam and I met at IIT Kharagpur and became close friends long before we became co-founders. What pulled us into building together was a shared frustration: the biggest problems around us weren't hidden — they were so normalized that nobody saw them anymore.

Dining out was the perfect example. Waving down staff to order, waiting for the bill, restaurants running on disconnected tools with zero memory of their customers — everyone had accepted this as just "how restaurants work." We couldn't unsee it. The entire offline dining experience was broken, and because it had always been broken, no one was fixing it.

We decided to become founders because these status-quo problems don't get solved by incumbents — they require someone naive enough to question the default. That conviction became Explorex.

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
\~90% of Indian retail happens in person, yet offline venues have no memory of their customers. A restaurant that has served someone fifty times knows less about them than an e-commerce site they visited once. This is the core problem: offline commerce is data-blind.

For restaurants, this means running on disconnected tools — one system for billing, another for reservations, spreadsheets for everything else — with no way to know who their customers are, what they love, or why they stopped coming. For diners, it means friction everywhere: flagging down staff to order, waiting for the bill, and a dining experience that hasn't fundamentally changed in decades.

It's a big problem because of the sheer scale of what's being left on the table. Food services in India is a massive market, and it operates with almost none of the intelligence that transformed online commerce. Delivery platforms captured the \~10% of eating that happens at home; the 90% that happens inside venues remains a black box.

We decided to work on it because the problem was obvious but invisible — it had been the status quo for so long that nobody questioned it. We realized that solving it requires owning both sides: the restaurant's operating system and the consumer's touchpoint. That's hard, which is exactly why it hasn't been done — and why it becomes an irreplicable moat once you do.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
Our vision is to build the memory layer for physical commerce — starting with dining.

If we truly succeed, walking into a restaurant will feel like the internet already works: the venue knows you, the experience is personalized, ordering and paying are frictionless, and an AI concierge (Elara) guides you to the best possible experience before you even decide where to go. Discovery, decision, and transaction collapse into one intelligent layer.

For restaurants, success means every independent venue in India operates with the data sophistication of an e-commerce giant — understanding their customers, optimizing their menus, and reaching high-intent diners directly instead of renting them from aggregators at punishing take rates. Think Shopify for restaurants: infrastructure that makes the merchant more powerful, not more dependent.

And dining is just the beachhead. The same problem — physical venues with no memory of their customers — exists across all of offline retail. If we win dining, we become the intelligence layer for offline commerce broadly: the UPI of physical retail operations, a shared infrastructure that makes the real world as smart as the digital one.

The world that results is one where the 90% of commerce that happens in person is no longer invisible — where physical businesses finally compete on equal footing with digital ones.
